newsitem.title: USA: KinderCare to relocate to Portland, Ore..
newsitem.headline: KinderCare to relocate to Portland, Ore..

text.p: KinderCare Learning Centres Inc. said Tuesday it will relocate its corporate headquarters from Montgomery, Ala. to Portland, Ore.
The company said it was making the move so it could more effectively support the educational quality and growth of its 1,151 child care centres.

Chief Executive David Johnson, who lives in Portland, said the decision to relocate the headquarters and reorganize management was made in consultation with the company's majority shareholder, Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co.

KinderCare provides daycare services for children aged six weeks to 12 years through company-owned operations, corporate-based facilities, after-school programmes and child care management agreements.

The relocation will be carried out in several phases throughout 1997 and possibly into early 1998. The company said it has begun a search for a new headquarters site in Portland, and expects to have found one by the end of March.
Separately, a group led by Tweedy Browne Co. LP, a New York investment adviser, said it has reduced its stake in KinderCare to 428,855 common shares or 2.17 percent from 5.03 percent previously.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the group said it sold 677,490 common between Feb. 14 and 18 at $19 per share.
The investment advisers sold their stock due to a tender offer by Kohlberg, Kravis, to purchase the outstanding shares for $19 per share.
